hero.title: Quick Start Guide
hero.description: Start with API keys, then use the SDK or direct API calls. Open the reference page for complete method and query documentation.

apiKeys.label: 01 / AUTH
apiKeys.title: API Keys
apiKeys.desc: Create, scope, rotate, and revoke workspace API keys for secure integrations.

sdk.label: 02 / SDK
sdk.title: SDK
sdk.desc: Use @layerum-team/rag-sdk for entities, uploads, ingestion wait, and query workflows.

api.label: 03 / API
api.title: API
api.desc: Explore public /v1 endpoints, capabilities, scopes, and request/response behavior.

install.title: Installation
install.desc: Install the official SDK package from npm.

client.title: Initialize the Client
client.desc: Initialize LayerumClient with your workspace API key.

mcpCli.title: MCP and CLI
mcpCli.desc: Use Layerum from a terminal or an AI assistant. The CLI and MCP server sign in with your own Layerum account through OAuth, so they are for people and AI assistants. The SDK uses workspace API keys (lyr_wk_*) and is for server integrations.

install.title: Install
install.desc: Install the CLI globally. Requires Node 20 or newer.

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.desc: Set the URLs of your Layerum server, then sign in. layerum login opens your browser and signs you in with OAuth. On SSH or in a container, use layerum login --code: open the printed URL on any device, authorize, and paste the code.

assistants.title: Connect an AI assistant
assistants.desc: Register the MCP server with your assistant. The assistant signs in through its login tool the first time it needs Layerum. Claude Code:
assistants.othersDesc: Other MCP clients: add this to the client's MCP configuration. It works with clients that accept the mcpServers format, such as Cursor and Claude Desktop.

sandbox.desc: Try our interactive playground to test API calls in real-time without writing a single line of local code.
